M01.name: k3
rows: 1. R-1 How do I set hours? Decided: Use one DUE_HOURS_<PRIORITY> variable per priority, in positive whole hours. Otherwise: Use one JSON setting, requiring operators to format the whole policy as JSON.
2. R-2 Is a ticket overdue at exactly its due timestamp? Decided: It becomes overdue once the clock passes that timestamp. Otherwise: Include equality and show the ticket one millisecond sooner.

3. R-3 How do I prepare a legacy file? Decided: Run an offline backfill against DATA_FILE using the existing stored priority, then enable. Otherwise: Auto-backfill during normal startup, coupling activation to the first migration write.

M02.name: k4
rows: 1. R-2 How does the help desk set the hours without a code change, and how large may they be? Decided: Four environment variables DUE_HOURS_URGENT/HIGH/NORMAL/LOW, whole hours from 1 to 87600 (ten years), read at start; unset keeps 4/24/72/168; a value outside that range or not a number stops the service at start naming the variable. Otherwise: A hours file (JSON) the service reads at start: adds a file to manage; or no upper bound, which lets a huge value crash ticket creation.

2. R-5 What does overdue=false or another value of overdue do? Decided: overdue=false means no filter; any other value is rejected 400 in the error envelope; unknown values of other parameters are still ignored as today. Otherwise: Treat every value other than true as no filter: fewer errors for clients, but a typo like overdue=ture silently lists every ticket.

3. R-6 When do the existing production tickets get their due times, given the switch is turned on only afterwards? Decided: At the first start of the new release on the data file, whether DUE_TIMES is on or off; the file is saved at once if any ticket was backfilled; operators deploy with DUE_TIMES off, check the file holds due, then set on. Otherwise: A separate one-time migration command operators run: one more step to remember and a service that would start without due times.

4. R-7 Which values of DUE_TIMES switch due times on? Decided: Only the exact value on; unset, empty or anything else (even ON or 1) leaves them off and the service answers as today. Otherwise: Accept on/ON/1/true: friendlier, but a stray value could expose due times early.

5. R-8 What happens to due times when operators roll back to 1.4.0 and later forward again? Decided: 1.4.0 starts and shows every ticket but drops due times at its first save; the new release backfills them again on the next start from created and the hours then configured. Documented for operators. Otherwise: Add a second version-1 field or sidecar file that 1.4.0 preserves: keeps original due times across a rollback but is a larger change to the format with no way for 1.4.0 to preserve it.

6. R-7 Does the command line show due times? Decided: No: bin/tickets.js, its table and `list --raw` stay exactly as today, with the flag on or off. Otherwise: Show due in `show` when DUE_TIMES=on: operators see it, but the command line would need to read the switch and the request does not ask for it.

M03.name: s1
rows: 1. R-2 How does the help desk change the hours? Decided: Operators set DUE_HOURS_URGENT, DUE_HOURS_HIGH, DUE_HOURS_NORMAL, DUE_HOURS_LOW in the service's environment and restart; unset means 4/24/72/168; a bad value stops start with a message naming it. Each value must be a whole number from 1 to 100000 hours, else start stops. Otherwise: A settings file or an API to edit hours live; it would add a new file or endpoint to maintain.

2. R-5 Is a ticket due exactly now overdue, and what does overdue=false do? Decided: Overdue means due strictly before now; overdue=true narrows the list; overdue=false or any other value gets a 400 invalid error. Otherwise: Accept overdue=false as 'only tickets not overdue'; it would add a second filter meaning.

3. R-7 What happens with DUE_TIMES unset, off or misspelt? Decided: Only the exact value on switches it on; anything else acts as off: no due in answers and overdue ignored. The service still stores due times in the data file. Otherwise: Refuse to start on an unknown value; a typo would stop the service instead of silently staying off.

4. R-6 When do existing tickets receive due times and what hours are used? Decided: At the first start of the new release, whatever DUE_TIMES says, using the hours set at that moment; the file is rewritten once with no audit entries. Otherwise: A separate migration command run by operators before the switch; it adds a step that can be forgotten.

5. R-8 What do operators lose by rolling back? Decided: 1.4.0 starts and shows every ticket, but its next save drops the due times; the next upgrade recomputes them from created time and priority with the hours then in force. Otherwise: Keep due in a side file that 1.4.0 never touches; it adds a second file to back up.

6. R-2 What is the largest number of hours accepted? Decided: 100000 hours (about 11 years); a larger value stops the service at start with a message naming the variable. Otherwise: No limit; an absurd value would make a due time that is not a valid date and fail at ticket creation.

M04.name: d4
rows: 1. R-1 How do I change the hours? Decided: Set SLA_HOURS_URGENT, SLA_HOURS_HIGH, SLA_HOURS_NORMAL or SLA_HOURS_LOW to positive whole hours. Otherwise: Use a single JSON environment value.
2. R-2 Is a ticket overdue exactly at its due time? Decided: It is overdue only after that instant. Otherwise: Count it at the exact instant as overdue.

3. R-3 How do I prepare the data file? Decided: Run the one-shot backfill with the service stopped, then enable the feature. Enabled startup also fills missing dues before listening. Otherwise: Rely entirely on startup backfill.
4. R-2 What happens with other overdue query values? Decided: Only the literal true activates the extra filter. Otherwise: Reject other values with 400.

M05.name: k1
rows: 1. R-1 Should the greeting end with a newline? Decided: The greeting appears on one complete line. Otherwise: Omit the newline so the next terminal output starts on the same line.

M06.name: d2
rows: 1. R-1 How do operators enter the hours? Decided: One positive whole-hour variable per priority. Otherwise: A JSON setting updates all priorities as one value.
2. R-2 Does the exact deadline count as overdue? Decided: It counts once the clock is later than the deadline. Otherwise: Count the deadline instant itself as overdue.

3. R-3 How do existing files get prepared before enabling? Decided: Run one offline migration command, then enable the switch. Otherwise: Start a preparatory release that migrates its file during startup.

M07.name: d1
rows: 1. R-1 How do operators override the response hours? Decided: Set positive whole hours in DUE_HOURS_<PRIORITY> at startup. Otherwise: A single JSON environment variable would require supplying a mapping.
2. R-2 When is a ticket past due? Decided: A ticket is overdue strictly after its timestamp. Otherwise: An inclusive boundary would surface the ticket at the exact due instant.

3. R-2 What changes for CLI users? Decided: The human list and show can display due with the flag on. Raw output stays at four fields. Otherwise: Adding a fifth raw field would change the column contract for scripts.

4. R-3 When does existing data get filled? Decided: The first new startup fills missing values before listening, even with the flag off. Otherwise: A separate offline migration would add an operator command.

M08.name: h1
rows: 1. R-1 Should the printed greeting end with a newline? Decided: The greeting is one line ending in a newline. Otherwise: Omit the trailing newline, which would leave the next terminal prompt on the same line.

M09.name: h2
rows: 1. R-1 Should the greeting end with a newline? Decided: The greeting appears as one complete line followed by a newline. Otherwise: Write the greeting without a newline, leaving the next terminal prompt on the same line.

M10.name: d3
rows: 1. R-1 How do operators override the hours? Decided: Use one DUE_HOURS_<PRIORITY> environment setting per priority, with positive whole hours. Otherwise: Use a separate configuration file that the operator edits and distributes.
2. R-2 Does a ticket count as overdue at the exact due instant? Decided: It counts from the first instant after due. Otherwise: Include tickets at the exact due instant.

3. R-3 How do operators populate deadlines before activation? Decided: Stop the writer, run an explicit backfill, then start with the flag on. Otherwise: Run migration automatically before the new server listens.

M11.name: k2
rows: 1. R-1 How do operators configure hours? Decided: Set DUE_HOURS_URGENT, DUE_HOURS_HIGH, DUE_HOURS_NORMAL or DUE_HOURS_LOW to positive whole hours; empty uses defaults. Otherwise: Use a JSON map setting.

2. R-2 What happens at the deadline and for other values? Decided: Only the literal true requests the filter, using a strictly past deadline and narrowing the existing listing. Otherwise: Treat exact due time as overdue and reject other values.

3. R-3 How do operators prepare and reveal deadlines? Decided: Run the offline command, then start with DUE_TIMES=on. An incomplete persisted file blocks enabled startup. Otherwise: Backfill as part of enabled startup before listening.
4. R-3 Where does the CLI show deadlines? Decided: Human list and show include due when enabled; the raw report stays stable. Otherwise: Make all CLI output add a column.

5. R-4 How can a rollback preserve original due values if 1.4.0 writes? Decided: Keep a pre-rollback snapshot and supply it to the migration on roll-forward; merge only matching deadlines and calculate for other tickets. Otherwise: Allow 1.4.0 writes to discard previously assigned deadlines.

M12.name: d6
rows: 1. R-1 How do operators set response hours? Decided: Use DUE_HOURS_URGENT, DUE_HOURS_HIGH, DUE_HOURS_NORMAL and DUE_HOURS_LOW for positive whole hours. Otherwise: Use a single JSON settings variable, requiring an operator to edit a JSON object.

2. R-3 Is a ticket overdue at the exact deadline? Decided: It enters the overdue list once the deadline has passed. Existing filters still apply. Otherwise: Include the ticket at equality, changing results at the exact timestamp.

3. R-4 What command prepares the data? Decided: Startup prepares missing deadlines before opening the port, including startup with the flag off. Otherwise: Use a separate offline migration command, requiring a separate operator invocation.

M13.name: d5
rows: 1. R-1 How are response hours configured? Decided: Set DUE_HOURS_URGENT, DUE_HOURS_HIGH, DUE_HOURS_NORMAL or DUE_HOURS_LOW to positive whole hours. Otherwise: Use one JSON environment value for all priorities.

2. R-2 What happens with other overdue values and existing filters? Decided: Only exact true activates it. The filter intersects the existing status/priority result before paging. Otherwise: Reject values other than true and false.

3. R-3 How does rollout populate the file? Decided: Run npm run backfill:due while the writer is stopped. Enabled startup also fills any missing deadlines before serving. Otherwise: Require a separate backfill and refuse startup when any value is missing.
4. R-2 What changes in the CLI? Decided: Human list and show display due with the flag on; raw output keeps its four-column contract. Otherwise: Show due only in HTTP.
